name: Ard Macha

attributes.attribute: the heights of Emain Macha, the name behind the city of Armagh
the mythical capital of Ulster, today's Navan Fort

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Ard Macha is an Irish name for the heights of Emain Macha. The name of Armagh in today's Northern Ireland derives from Ard Macha, the heights of the goddess Macha. Emain Macha is a late Bronze Age hillfort in County Armagh. It is the mythical capital of the ancient province of Ulster. One tradition tells of the warrior queen Macha Mong Rua. She marked out a vast hillfort with a brooch and forced her captives to build it. Today the site is called Navan Fort. It is a heritage site equal in stature to Cruachan, Tara, and Knockaulin.
